mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a decline in economic demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where real GDP dropped by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increased by more than 2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, suggests a stable economic environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls decreased by more than 100,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) both increase by more than 5% month-over-month, it signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and construction activity boost corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 5% MoM
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both housing starts and real final sales increased by more than 5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it indicates a tight labor market with high interest rates, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as borrowing costs rise and wage pressures increase.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the federal funds rate was above 4% and the unemployment rate was below 4%.
